title: Model-based redesign of global transcription regulation.
assessment: Empirical transcriptional perturbation comparison; independent split not established in inspected text.

title: Plato's cave algorithm: inferring functional signaling networks from early gene expression shadows.
assessment: Intervention-based early expression prediction; predictive split and benchmark details need report-level verification.

title: Identifying biological network structure, predicting network behavior, and classifying network state with High Dimensional Model Representation (HDMR).
assessment: DREAM training/test comparisons for phosphoproteins and cytokines; network recovery is distinct from response prediction.

title: De novo inference of systems-level mechanistic models of development from live-imaging-based phenotype analysis.
assessment: 310 embryos across wild type and 20 RNAi targets anchor developmental inference; unseen-intervention separation not established.

title: Epigenetic landscapes explain partially reprogrammed cells and identify key reprogramming genes.
assessment: Known reprogramming TF combinations used as retrospective biological anchors; prospective prediction performance not established.

title: Dynamics of embryonic stem cell differentiation inferred from single-cell transcriptomics show a series of transitions through discrete cell states.
assessment: Simulated transcription-factor effects on discrete states; held-out perturbation evaluation not established from the inspected passages.

title: Bayesian Networks Predict Neuronal Transdifferentiation.
assessment: Empirical source/target profiles support simulated reprogramming; an independent dataset can still be used to learn the model and is not automatically a held-out test.

title: Dr.VAE: improving drug response prediction via modeling of drug perturbation effects.
assessment: Cell-line-grouped repeated cross-validation; molecular response and viability classification are separate evaluation endpoints.

title: Optimal-Transport Analysis of Single-Cell Gene Expression Identifies Developmental Trajectories in Reprogramming.
assessment: Predicts distributions at withheld intermediate timepoints using both adjacent times; evidence for interpolation, not future-only forecasting.

title: scGen predicts single-cell perturbation responses.
assessment: Held-out stimulated cell types; PCA baseline and gene-distribution comparisons. Raw-expression correlation requires separate response-difference assessment.

title: Landscape inferred from gene expression data governs pluripotency in embryonic stem cells.
assessment: Parameter selection minimizes discrepancy against observed expression states; calibration and independent prediction need separation.

title: Generative modeling of single-cell time series with PRESCIENT enables prediction of cell trajectories with interventions.
assessment: Day 4 withheld between observed training times; evaluation uses Wasserstein distance and lineage-fate metrics.

title: Personalized single-cell networks: a framework to predict the response of any gene to any drug for any patient.
assessment: Cross-cell-line gene/drug map comparison; the reference is a derived RWR score, not a direct matched cellular outcome.

title: DeepVelo: Single-cell transcriptomic deep velocity field learning with neural ordinary differential equations.
assessment: Simulated neuronal fate dynamics; independent timepoint or perturbation test not established in inspected passages.

title: IQCELL: A platform for predicting the effect of gene perturbations on developmental trajectories using single-cell RNA-seq data.
assessment: Perturbation comparisons plus GRN AUPRC; distinguish response validation from network-edge recovery.

title: NETISCE: a network-based tool for cell fate reprogramming.
assessment: Reproduces previously simulated and experimentally observed reprogramming results; prospective validation not established.

title: Predicting drug polypharmacology from cell morphology readouts using variational autoencoder latent space arithmetic.
assessment: 80/10/10 data split stratified by plate/cell line distributes MOAs across folds; this alone does not test unseen MOAs.

title: scTenifoldKnk: An efficient virtual knockout tool for gene function predictions via single-cell gene regulatory network perturbation.
assessment: Virtual knockout compared with experimental knockout signatures; cell subsampling robustness is not independent animal replication.

title: Biologically informed variational autoencoders allow predictive modeling of genetic and drug-induced perturbations.
assessment: Predictive ontology-guided perturbation examples; repeated training stability is distinct from external validation.

title: Dissecting cell identity via network inference and in silico gene perturbation.
assessment: CellOracle simulates TF perturbations and experimentally tests zebrafish phenotypes; GRN AUROC evaluates a different task from phenotype prediction.

title: Gene knockout inference with variational graph autoencoder learning single-cell gene regulatory networks.
assessment: Random edge split evaluates GRN reconstruction; knockout benchmark includes simulated data. Separate edge prediction from real response validation.

title: Generative modeling of single-cell gene expression for dose-dependent chemical perturbations.
assessment: Dose-conditioned expression prediction and cross-study examples; assess expression change as well as R2 over gene means.

title: Homogeneous Space Construction and Projection for Single-Cell Expression Prediction Based on Deep Learning.
assessment: All perturbed cells of one cell type withheld; three baseline methods and three datasets compared.

title: Learning perturbation-inducible cell states from observability analysis of transcriptome dynamics.
assessment: Data-driven dynamics and sensor selection; many reported differential genes use unadjusted significance and do not establish a validated perturbation predictor by themselves.

title: Learning single-cell perturbation responses using neural optimal transport.
assessment: CellOT maps control to treatment distributions and tests unseen patients/contexts; MMD supplements mean-expression metrics.

title: Predicting cellular responses to complex perturbations in high-throughput screens.
assessment: 28 held-out covariate/dose splits; linear and random baselines. Unseen combinations and unseen single perturbations must be distinguished.

title: SCENIC+: single-cell multiomic inference of enhancers and gene regulatory networks.
assessment: RF-based TF perturbation and phenotype-switch simulation present; eGRN recovery benchmarking is not equivalent to unseen intervention validation.

title: Transfer learning enables predictions in network biology.
assessment: Geneformer performs in-silico intervention and reported cardiomyocyte experiments; classification cross-validation is a separate endpoint.

title: scDisInFact: disentangled learning for integration and prediction of multi-batch multi-condition single-cell RNA-sequencing data.
assessment: In-sample and out-of-sample evaluations reported separately; cell-random split provides weaker evidence than omitted conditions.

title: BioDSNN: a dual-stream neural network with hybrid biological knowledge integration for multi-gene perturbation response prediction.
assessment: Unseen-gene categories specified for single and paired perturbations; top-DE-gene MSE compared with other methods.

title: BuDDI: Bulk Deconvolution with Domain Invariance to predict cell-type-specific perturbations from bulk.
assessment: Perturbation prediction and pseudobulk deconvolution; sex counterfactuals lack matched individual ground truth and should remain exploratory.

title: CODEX: COunterfactual Deep learning for the in silico EXploration of cancer cell line perturbations.
assessment: Explicit withheld single and paired perturbations with proxy modelling; drug synergy and transcriptome tasks separated.

title: CRISPR-GEM: A Novel Machine Learning Model for CRISPR Genetic Target Discovery and Evaluation.
assessment: CRISPR-GEM predicts transcriptome shifts including cartilage examples; reported training fit does not establish unseen intervention validity.

title: Cell reprogramming design by transfer learning of functional transcriptional networks.
assessment: Data-driven intervention optimization against known reprogramming approaches; independent test separation not established in inspected text.

title: EnhancerNet: a predictive model of cell identity dynamics through enhancer selection.
assessment: Enhancer-based state dynamics and empirical developmental examples; held-out response validation not established.

title: FateNet: an integration of dynamical systems and deep learning for cell fate prediction.
assessment: Synthetic bifurcation trajectories train the model; biological data test transferability, rather than direct evidence of repair intervention prediction.

title: GRouNdGAN: GRN-guided simulation of single-cell RNA-seq data using causal generative adversarial networks.
assessment: Generative and virtual-knockout outputs present; synthetic GRN benchmark performance does not establish real intervention generalization.

title: Modeling and predicting single-cell multi-gene perturbation responses with scLAMBDA.
assessment: Splits by perturbation targets and conditions, with separate validation; single/pair generalization and genetic-interaction endpoints.

title: Predicting single-cell cellular responses to perturbations using cycle consistency learning.
assessment: Drug-level held-out conditions reported; transcriptomic and proteomic endpoints compared with baselines.

title: Predicting transcriptional outcomes of novel multigene perturbations with GEARS.
assessment: GEARS distinguishes 0/2, 1/2 and 2/2 unseen target genes; top-20 DEG error and response correlations.

title: Predicting transcriptional responses to novel chemical perturbations using deep generative model for drug discovery.
assessment: Compound and cell-line splits; log-fold-change correlations provide response-specific evaluation.

title: The manatee variational autoencoder model for predicting gene expression alterations caused by transcription factor perturbations.
assessment: Interpretable TF-conditioned generation; reconstruction and imputation effects do not alone validate perturbation responses.

title: Transfer learning of condition-specific perturbation in gene interactions improves drug response prediction.
assessment: Perturbed expression modelling and repeated cross-validation; exact split unit needs verification.

title: Uncovering underlying physical principles and driving forces of cell differentiation and reprogramming from single-cell transcriptomics.
assessment: Data-constrained landscape and in-silico interventions; empirical held-out intervention agreement not established.

title: scCross: a deep generative model for unifying single-cell multi-omics with seamless integration, cross-modal generation, and in silico exploration.
assessment: Cross-modal in-silico perturbation present; missing-modality generation benchmark differs from intervention-response validation.

title: scNODE : generative model for temporal single cell transcriptomic data prediction.
assessment: Tests unmeasured timepoints with distribution shift and Wasserstein distance.

title: scPRAM accurately predicts single-cell gene expression perturbation response based on attention mechanism.
assessment: Whole species response held out in transfer tests; donor independence and differential-response accuracy need distinct evaluation.

title: Cell-GraphCompass: modeling single cells with graph structure foundation model.
assessment: Uses GEARS condition splits and compares expression and delta correlations with GEARS/scGPT.

title: CellFM: a large-scale foundation model pre-trained on transcriptomics of 100 million human cells.
assessment: Forward and reverse perturbation tasks reported; random combinatorial split is not proof of new-cell-type generalization.

title: CellNavi predicts genes directing cellular transitions by learning a gene graph-enhanced cell state manifold.
assessment: Clusters and multigene conditions withheld; inverse target prediction is the primary outcome.

title: CoupleVAE: coupled variational autoencoders for predicting perturbational single-cell RNA sequencing data.
assessment: Inspected PBMC experiment uses cell-random i.i.d. splits across eight donors; donor independence cannot be inferred from cell counts.

title: DANSE: a pipeline for dynamic modelling of time-series multi-omics data.
assessment: Fitted temporal model permits interventions; experimental testing of suggested regulators remains a proposed step.

title: Data-driven inference of Boolean networks from transcriptomes to predict cellular differentiation and reprogramming.
assessment: Ensembles across binarization choices and replicates; independent response-validation details need verification.

title: Deciphering hierarchical regulatory network of cell fate via an epigenetics-informed heterogeneous graph transformer on single-cell multi-omics data.
assessment: In-silico perturbation component present; cis/trans edge benchmarking does not establish downstream response prediction.

title: Fast and scalable Wasserstein-1 neural optimal transport solver for single-cell perturbation prediction.
assessment: Unseen-cell-type transfer compared with identity, observed-target and learned-transport baselines.

title: Gradient-aware modeling advances AI-driven prediction of genetic perturbation effects.
assessment: Unseen perturbations from the same screen; multiple datasets and gene-wise response metrics.

title: Hybrid deep learning-mechanistic modeling of cellular dynamics from a spatiotemporal single-cell atlas.
assessment: Spatial bins held out; teacher-guided mechanistic editing is distinct from independent organism or experimental perturbation validation.

title: LazyNet: Interpretable ODE Modeling of Sparse CRISPR Single-Cell Screens Reveals New Biological Insights.
assessment: Guide/target grouping and batch-aware splits reported; check target overlap across guides when judging unseen-gene generalization.

title: Mouse-Geneformer: A deep learning model for mouse single-cell transcriptome and its cross-species utility.
assessment: Cross-species in-silico intervention and disease typing; wet-lab response validation not established in inspected text.

title: PerturbNet predicts single-cell responses to unseen chemical and genetic perturbations.
assessment: Five unseen-chemical splits, stereoisomer exclusion and DEG metrics; remains predominantly reference-cell-line evidence.

title: Predicting cell morphological responses to perturbations using generative modeling.
assessment: Generative morphological perturbation model with multiple image baselines; batch correction is separate from unseen-drug prediction.

title: Spatia: Multimodal Model for Prediction and Generation of Spatial Cell Phenotypes.
assessment: Conditional phenotype generation; held-out feature reconstruction alone does not validate interventions.

title: VIP-OT: Dissecting Single-Cell Biochemical State Dynamics under Perturbation via Vibrational Painting and Optimal Transport.
assessment: Within-drug control-cell cross-validation and biochemical spectra metrics; not an unseen-drug test.

title: scELMo: Embeddings from Language Models are Good Learners for Single-cell Data Analysis.
assessment: Language-derived embeddings used in chemical/genetic response prediction; annotation metrics excluded from response synthesis.

title: scOTM: A Deep Learning Framework for Predicting Single-Cell Perturbation Responses with Large Language Models.
assessment: Stimulated cell type fully held out; squared correlation and gene-wise intervals require separation from independent-context uncertainty.

title: scPerb: Predict single-cell perturbation via style transfer-based variational autoencoder.
assessment: Perturbation prediction compared with baselines; high raw-expression R2 alone cannot establish effect-size recovery.

title: scVAEDer: integrating deep diffusion models and variational autoencoders for single-cell transcriptomics analysis.
assessment: Unseen-perturbation evaluation reported; exact withheld unit and metric completeness require verification.

title: A Neural-Network-Free Calibration Matches or Beats Deep Single-Cell Perturbation Response Models Across Four Datasets.
assessment: Matched access to held-out control inputs; observed stimulated groups excluded from training.

title: A generative framework for predicting cellular morphological and transcriptomic perturbation responses.
assessment: Compound-level split with chemical similarity constraint and response-difference endpoints.

title: A transcription factor regulatory atlas for activity inference and perturbation prediction.
assessment: Signed-prior prediction compared with observed TF-knockdown responses; inverse TF-activity recovery is a separate task.

title: CFM-GP: unified conditional flow matching to learn gene perturbation across cell types.
assessment: Whole-species response transfer; expression ranking statistics supplement response-difference evaluation.

title: CardamomOT: A mechanistic optimal transport-based framework for gene regulatory network inference, trajectory reconstruction and generative modeling.
assessment: Calibrated generative and unseen-perturbation simulation; inspected network benchmark is synthetic, so empirical response validation requires verification.

title: Celcomen: spatial causal disentanglement for single-cell and tissue perturbation modeling.
assessment: Spatial Tgfbr2 perturbation predicts transcriptomes; context-specific lesions and experimental perturbation source define applicability.

title: CellPolaris: Transfer Learning for Gene Regulatory Network Construction to Guide Cell State Transitions.
assessment: Learned GRNs support TF simulation; cross-tissue GRN AUROC does not directly measure cellular-response accuracy.

title: DECANT: decoupling mechanism from context in single-cell drug perturbation representation.
assessment: Drug-group split; bag-level response-difference metrics across seeds. Seeds quantify algorithm variation, not biological replication.

title: DestinyNet: A deep-learning framework for cell-fate analysis from lineage-tracing single-cell RNA sequencing data.
assessment: Clones, rather than cells, used as split units in specified lineage-tracing tasks.

title: Dynamic graph prior-guided latent adaptation for generalizable single-cell perturbation response prediction.
assessment: Explicit unseen-cell-type and joint unseen-drug scenarios; held-out controls are test inputs.

title: Enhancing cross-context generalization in drug perturbation prediction with a multimodal conditional diffusion framework.
assessment: Drug, cell-line and stricter cell-cluster splits; delta-expression and directional DEG endpoints.

title: Illuminating cell states by a comprehensive and interpretable single cell foundation model.
assessment: GEARS-integrated perturbation prediction; matched baseline conditions and delta metrics reported.

title: Learning stochastic dynamics and cell-fate landscapes from single-cell snapshots via optimal transport.
assessment: Generative stochastic cell dynamics; simulated-noise robustness does not establish empirical intervention generalization.

title: MultiPert: An adversarial alignment and dual attention framework for single-cell multi-omics perturbation prediction.
assessment: Within-condition cell splits and leave-one-perturbation-out tests are both reported and must be separated.

title: Multiscale learning of gene network-driven phenotypic dynamics of single cells.
assessment: Seven held-out timepoints, Wasserstein error and repeated random seeds; reconstruction and forecast endpoints distinguished.

title: PHAROS: turning single-cell perturbation models into target-directed drug-combination screens.
assessment: External two-drug dataset but shared A549 identity; transfer is across datasets/combined states, not unseen cell identity.

title: PertAdapt: unlocking single-cell foundation models for genetic perturbation prediction via condition-sensitive adaptation.
assessment: All cells of each perturbation condition assigned together; single/pair unseen-target classes reported.

title: Pre-Existing Heterogeneity Predicts Rare Proteostasis-Stress Programs Across Diverse Perturbations.
assessment: Grouped task/cell-line/perturbation/dataset holdouts and fold-fitted QC residualization; output is a stress programme, not an entire cell.

title: Predicting Single-Cell Perturbation Responses Across Biological Contexts With a Deep Generative Model Integrating Optimal Transport.
assessment: Context-level paired analyses after averaging seeds; explicit held-out patients/species/cell types.

title: Prediction of parsimonious and temporally sensitive sets of cell fate engineering transcription factors with IMCell.
assessment: Experimental reprogramming references and synthetic dynamics support target selection; held-out TF classification is distinct from response validation.

title: Predictive control of human pancreatic cell fate using a digital model of in vitro differentiation.
assessment: Digital pancreatic differentiation model executes interventions; in-vivo/in-vitro atlas comparison does not by itself validate predicted intervention effects.

title: RegFormer: a single-cell foundation model powered by gene regulatory hierarchies.
assessment: Perturbation task uses GEARS protocol and differential-expression metrics; drug sensitivity task is assessed separately.

title: Scouter predicts transcriptional responses to genetic perturbations with large language model embeddings.
assessment: Unseen genetic perturbation comparison with task-specific and foundation models; response distributions also evaluated.

title: Temporal AI model predicts drivers of cell state trajectories across human aging.
assessment: Temporal generation and in-silico age-associated interventions; pretraining scale does not establish intervention validity.

title: Unveiling gene perturbation effects through gene regulatory networks inference from single-cell transcriptomic data.
assessment: External species/technology dataset supports GRN/dynamic reconstruction; high reconstruction correlation is not an unseen intervention metric.

title: pertTF: context-aware AI modeling for genome-scale and cross-system perturbation prediction.
assessment: Unseen-cell-type, unseen-target and combined generalization plus orthogonal primary-islet data reported.

title: scBalFlow: a staged flow matching framework for imbalanced single-cell drug perturbation prediction.
assessment: Dose/DEG and held-out cell-type evaluation; comparators unable to represent new identities were omitted in that task.

title: scGPA: an LLM-assisted workflow for directional virtual gene perturbation analysis from single-cell transcriptomes.
assessment: 304 targets across five Perturb-seq datasets; directional top-gene correctness evaluated. Exact leakage controls need verification.

title: scLDM: a conditional diffusion framework for single-cell perturbation prediction.
assessment: Held-out paired perturbations and DEG comparisons; reference-baseline strength and all-gene correlation assessed separately.

title: Evaluating the Utilities of Foundation Models in Single-Cell Data Analysis.
assessment: Includes perturbation prediction; annotation dataset splits must not be reused as proof of perturbation-task separation.

title: AUPRC: a metric for evaluating the performance of in-silico perturbation methods in identifying differentially expressed genes.
assessment: Metric study focuses on DEG precision-recall under class imbalance; this supports endpoint selection, not a clinical certainty grade.

title: Benchmarking foundation cell models for post-perturbation RNA-seq prediction.
assessment: Uses multiple Perturb-seq datasets and reports expression, response-difference and target-excluded variants of correlation.

title: Deep-learning-based gene perturbation effect prediction does not yet outperform simple linear baselines.
assessment: Unseen perturbation evaluation includes explicit linear/mean baselines; negative findings enter the synthesis.

title: What Do Single-Cell Models Already Know About Perturbations?
assessment: Cell-random splits for representation probing; limited support for novel-context intervention prediction.

title: A community machine learning challenge to predict the effects of gene perturbations on T cell differentiation for cancer immunotherapy.
assessment: Perturbation-level challenge and repeated cross-fold comparison; biological differentiation endpoint is explicit.

title: A systematic assessment of single-cell language model configurations.
assessment: Language-model configuration benchmark includes post-perturbation prediction and competitive simple baselines.

title: A systematic comparison of single-cell perturbation response prediction models.
assessment: Task-specific unseen conditions and response decomposition; evaluate each generalization setting separately.

title: Evaluating the learnability of single-cell large language models on multiple tasks.
assessment: Perturb-seq task included; classification dataset split shown in general text cannot establish the perturbation split.

title: Spurious correlation inflates performance in single-cell perturbation prediction.
assessment: Analytical and simulated assessment of shared-control bias in Pearson delta; important for metric interpretation.

title: Systema: a framework for evaluating genetic perturbation response prediction beyond systematic variation.
assessment: Reference-sensitive metrics and systematic variation analyzed; some comparators were not designed for the evaluated unseen-gene task.

title: Systematic evaluation of single-cell foundation model interpretability: attention-derived edge scores add no incremental value over gene-level features for perturbation-target prediction.
assessment: Model-head ablation and perturbation-target metrics test interpretability; no clinical intervention inference.

title: scArchon: a scalable benchmarking framework for assessing single-cell perturbation models.
assessment: Whole context left out across six datasets; transcriptomic and biological programme metrics assessed.

title: Network modeling predicts personalized gene expression and drug responses in valve myofibroblasts cultured with patient sera.
assessment: Patient-serum-conditioned myofibroblast output comparison; the clinical correlations do not establish clinical treatment benefit.

title: Gene regulatory network reconfiguration in direct lineage reprogramming.
assessment: CellOracle screening of 180 active TFs followed by tests of selected reprogramming regulators; selection-stage and validation-stage evidence distinguished.

title: Deep learning-aided inter-species-comparison reveals shared and distinct molecular patterns in cynomolgus monkey and humans following non-specific T cell activation.
assessment: Cell-level split and baseline-trained species translation; no evidence here of held-out donors.

title: Discovering Candidate Anti-Aging Perturbations Using a Foundation Model for Gene Expression.
assessment: Donor-wise age-model evaluation is explicit; simulated anti-ageing interventions were not experimentally validated.

title: Counterfactual Diffusion Modeling Enables Spatially Targeted Reprogramming of Tissue Microenvironments.
assessment: Counterfactual spatial interventions are compared with observational clinical groups; test-cohort metadata also define concept vectors. Prospective intervention benefit not established.

title: Geneformer-guided multiomics integration identifies Pbx1 as a network hub of hematopoietic stem cell aging.
assessment: Geneformer-guided Pbx1 experiments and HSC phenotypes; source versions and model revisions reported.

title: Identification of SORT1 as a Key Regulator of Antigen Presentation in CD16+ Monocytes During Septic Shock via Multi-Omics and In Silico Gene Knockout Analysis.
assessment: Virtual SORT1 knockout provides network hypotheses; external diagnostic AUC is not validation of the simulated knockout.

title: Identification of diagnostic biomarkers for neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis via machine learning screening and single-cell virtual gene knockout validation.
assessment: Virtual knockout and animal expression measurements are present; biomarker concordance alone does not validate the knockout intervention.

title: In Silico Perturbation Identifies Transcription Factors as Protective Targets in HSPCs After Irradiation.
assessment: CellOracle predictions linked to celastrol after irradiation and Hsf1 knockdown; treatment timing and lineage-specific outcomes are explicit.

title: Integrative Single-Cell Transcriptomic, Mendelian Randomization and In Silico Perturbation Analyses Prioritize MUC20 as a Candidate Gene Associated with Osteoporosis and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in the Liver-Bone Axis.
assessment: MUC20 virtual perturbation is exploratory; Mendelian-randomization and cross-disease expression results are not perturbation-response tests.

title: Network Model to Predict Age-Related Transcriptional Reprogramming.
assessment: Predicted chondrocyte response compared with prior RNA-seq after conditioned media; a separate network mechanistic stratum may be needed.

title: PAH-former: Transfer learning for efficient discovery of pulmonary arterial hypertension-associated genes.
assessment: Geneformer target predictions tested by siRNA in pulmonary endothelial cells; independent expression data are supportive, not treatment outcomes.

title: Single‑Cell in silico Perturbation Uncovers a Ferroptosis Regulatory Network for Cigarette Smoke‑Induced Skin Aging and Identifies Dapivirine as a Candidate Agent.
assessment: Virtual overexpression/knockout generates skin-ageing hypotheses; enrichment is not experimental validation of the selected drug.

assessment: Explicit mechanistic VCell/whole-cell modelling lineage; excluded from modern AI evidence denominator.

assessment: Pseudocell Tracer predicts held-out cells; separate reconstruction from temporal extrapolation.

title: CellRank for directed single-cell fate mapping.
assessment: CellRank fate predictions supported by epithelial marker assessment after bleomycin; trajectories and intervention outcomes are distinct.

title: CoSpar identifies early cell fate biases from single-cell transcriptomic and lineage information.
assessment: CoSpar combines clonal information and transcriptomes to infer fate bias; clone-level validation needs separate extraction.

title: Mapping transcriptomic vector fields of single cells.
assessment: Dynamo reconstructs a vector field and simulates gene-wise interventions; evaluate kinetic reconstruction separately from predicted perturbations.

title: scREMOTE: Using multimodal single cell data to predict regulatory gene relationships and to build a computational cell reprogramming model.
assessment: scREMOTE simulates TF perturbations and long-term reprogramming; predicted expression is clipped to observed limits.

title: Disentanglement of single-cell data with biolord.
assessment: Biolord compares unseen single and paired genetic perturbations with GEARS and no-effect baselines.

title: Fatecode enables cell fate regulator prediction using classification-supervised autoencoder perturbation.
assessment: Fatecode perturbs latent cellular representations to prioritize regulators; classification fit does not alone validate the predicted interventions.

title: Large-scale foundation model on single-cell transcriptomics.
assessment: scFoundation includes perturbation prediction among several tasks; separate its response metrics from annotation and drug sensitivity.

title: OneSC: a computational platform for recapitulating cell state transitions.
assessment: OneSC simulates state transitions and compares myeloid perturbations with known experimental results.

title: Stochastic Modeling of Biophysical Responses to Perturbation.
assessment: Biophysical kinetics used to predict combined perturbation responses; random-noise substitutions serve as controls.

title: iGTP: learning interpretable cellular embedding for inferring biological mechanisms underlying single-cell transcriptomics.
assessment: iGTP includes an iGEARS perturbation prediction component; embedding interpretation is a different task.

title: scEMB: Learning context representation of genes based on large-scale single-cell transcriptomics
assessment: scEMB in-silico predictions compared with CRISPRi through embedding similarity; expression-change accuracy needs separate evaluation.

title: scGPT: toward building a foundation model for single-cell multi-omics using generative AI.
assessment: scGPT original response-prediction task is eligible; gene/cell representation tasks are not equivalent validation endpoints.

title: A deep generative model for deciphering cellular dynamics and in silico drug discovery in complex diseases.
assessment: UNAGI predicts perturbation responses with a PCLS treatment benchmark; disease-stage mapping is separated from response prediction.

title: ARTEMIS integrates autoencoders and Schrödinger Bridges to predict continuous dynamics of gene expression, cell population, and perturbation from time-series single-cell data.
assessment: ARTEMIS withholds an intermediate EMT timepoint and predicts distributions; this is not future-only extrapolation.

title: Computing hematopoiesis plasticity in response to genetic mutations and environmental stimulations.
assessment: Computational perturbations of hematopoietic TFs and pathways; the inspected source does not establish new experimental testing.

title: EpiAgent: foundation model for single-cell epigenomics.
